chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent me to Yemen, he said: 'O Ali! Do not fight anyone until you call him to Islam. And I swear by Allah, if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, were to guide one man through your hands, that is better for you than what the sun rises upon and sets upon, and his allegiance (walayah) would be yours.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam (the call to accept the faith)
key_terms.الْيَمَنِ: Yemen (the region where Imam Ali was sent)
key_terms.وَلَاؤُهُ: His allegiance/guardianship (referring to the spiritual and political bond with the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's instruction to Imam Ali regarding fighting and inviting to Islam in Yemen?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the strategic principle of *da'wah* preceding *qital*, establishing that military action is a last resort after inviting opponents to Islam. It underscores the immense spiritual value of individual guidance, noting that the guided person's *walayah* (allegiance) becomes the Imam's, a concept central to Shia political theology. This instruction reflects the Prophet's specific directive to Imam Ali during his mission to Yemen, prioritizing spiritual conquest over territorial expansion.
